title: Bank Deposit Incorrect-Amount Errors: Paloma's Make-Good Credit
content:
When an incorrect amount is found on a Bank Deposit transfer, Paloma puts its make-good credit into the transfer, booked as a credit for an incorrect-amount shortfall against the payout that came up short, and its amount is the make-good credit for that transfer rather than the bare shortfall.

## When it applies

An incorrect amount is found when Paloma's error-resolution team decides "error found" on the customer's notice that the recipient received less than the disclosed amount. The make-good credit is Paloma's own money.

## What the credit books

One make-good credit is booked on the transfer's ledger as a credit for an incorrect-amount shortfall, dated the day it is booked and pointing back to the payout that came up short. The transfer's ledger then carries Paloma's make-good credit for the incorrect amount, and the principal Paloma holds on the transfer rises by the amount credited. Nothing is sent to the customer or the recipient by the credit itself.

## Booking it: `book_shortfall_credit_979e59e7`

**Owner and invocation.** This is an agent-side tool. The agent unlocks `book_shortfall_credit_979e59e7` and then calls it. Each call books one make-good credit for an incorrect-amount shortfall.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `bank_transfer_id` | The reference number of the Bank Deposit transfer being made good, as returned by the Bank Deposit transfer lookup for this customer | identifier |
| `related_entry_id` | The reference number of the payout money movement that came up short, as returned by the Bank Deposit money-movement lookup for that transfer | identifier |
| `credit_amount_usd` | The amount Paloma credits, in US dollars | positive number with 2 decimal places (cents); recorded exactly as passed after rounding half up to 2 decimal places |

**Return.** A dictionary rendered as text with `ledger_entry_id` (the reference number of the new credit movement), `bank_transfer_id` (the transfer credited), `credited_usd` (the amount credited, US dollars with 2 decimal places), `credit_reason` (always `incorrect_amount_shortfall`), `entry_date` (the credit date, YYYY-MM-DD), `principal_held_usd` (the principal Paloma holds on the transfer afterwards, US dollars with 2 decimal places) and `status` (credited when the credit was booked).

## Points of judgement

- **The error-resolution team decided "no error" on the incorrect-amount notice.** No incorrect amount was found, so no make-good credit arises.
- **Against which payout is the credit booked?** Against the payout that came up short.
- **Does the credit itself pay the recipient?** No; it raises the principal Paloma holds on the transfer and sends nothing.
